content.comment_body: Hello, In the attached image you can see the current setup at home using a [product_name] [article_no] model (not sure about the exact version). Is it possible to extend this setup with another module, such as [article_no], to enable instructions over Wi-Fi? What would be required to achieve this? Thanks for your assistance.
The image shows a [product_name] power supply. It only provides power in and out and does not have any logic or software capabilities.

Hi, You can replace the existing [product_name] [article_no] with a newer [product_name] [article_no]. The newer module is compatible with the program from the older version. However, if you have any additional expansion modules connected to your current setup, they won’t work with the newer [product_name] [article_no]. If you want to keep using the older [article_no] and add the newer [article_no] for communication purposes, the only solution is to use I/O connections between the two modules. The older [article_no] does not support direct communication unless you have extra hardware, such as KNX modules, on both units. If you have KNX on your current module, you’ll need to add a KNX module to the newer one as well. If possible, replacing your current [product_name] [article_no] with a newer [product_name] [article_no] is the best solution in my opinion. Hope this helps.

analysis.insight_summary: Users are looking to upgrade an older [product_name] setup by integrating newer modules to enable Wi-Fi functionality and remote control. Main challenges revolve around hardware compatibility and connecting communication features to legacy systems.
analysis.user_expectations: The user wishes to expand their existing setup with a newer module to make remote control via Wi-Fi possible. They prefer an easy integration process that minimizes changes to current hardware.
